investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-25T20:04 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every remote-agents check. Because the failure happens at the very first network hop to the swarm backend — before agent creation can proceed — all downstream evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent. This is an eval-detected infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions failed: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has exhausted its credit balance. The OpenAI API returned error code "credit_balance_exhausted" with type "insufficient_quota", which caused the server-side image generation to abort. The SSE stream emitted a generation_error frame carrying this error message instead of completing with a generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure — no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed are [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message] — generation_completed is absent, and imageUrlPresent is false.
failed-check.evidence: The generation_error frame data.message contains the full OpenAI quota error JSON, confirming the upstream API rejected the request before image synthesis could complete.

expected-output.contract: The contract requires frameTypes to contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent to equal true — both violated as a direct consequence of the upstream quota error.
possibleCauses: Primary — OpenAI account credit balance is exhausted: The API key configured for the eval runner's image generation calls has no remaining prepaid credits, causing every call to /api/generate/image/stream to be rejected immediately with credit_balance_exhausted. This is the direct, evidence-backed cause.

Secondary — Wrong or expired API key configured for the eval environment: The key in use may belong to an account that has run out of credits or has been rotated/revoked, while a funded key exists elsewhere but is not wired to this eval runner environment.

Tertiary — Eval runner is using a model (gpt-image-2 or AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL override) that is billed against a quota-limited account tier: The model selection could be routing to a billing tier or sub-account with a separate, exhausted quota.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because the aura-gpt-5-5 model returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing 1 of 2 models to fail and violating the allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 contract assertions. The sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 passed cleanly, isolating the failure to the aura-gpt-5-5 provider path only.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-25T20:03:56Z). The error chain is: POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test → 502 bad_gateway → harness llm_error → API status 424 → error code provider_account_unavailable. The provider field and resolvedModel field in the result for aura-gpt-5-5 are both null, indicating the AURA runtime could not resolve or reach the provider at all. This is consistent with a transient or ongoing upstream provider connectivity issue on AURA's side, as stated in the error message itself. No eval infrastructure failure is indicated: all required evidence fields were present, the runner executed both models, and the contract machinery functioned correctly.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-25T20:04 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every remote-agents check. Because the failure happens at the very first network hop to the swarm backend — before agent creation can proceed — all downstream evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent.
